scope: The exact FE-355 claim derived from arXiv:2608.12880: in one preserved MCP-style agent-security campaign, the historical ATTACK_SUCCESS endpoint directly consumed a surface-derived adversarial-treatment flag, so holding an authorized two-tool behavioral record fixed while changing only that flag flips the class from benign success to attack success. Across the reconstructed 180 model-bound requests, 31 historical ATTACK_SUCCESS labels change when only the surface-derived flag is forced false; a treatment-blind reconstruction reclassifies 58 of 70 historical ATTACK_SUCCESS or HIJACK_ATTEMPT labels as authorized benign completions, while retaining three verified protected-data transfers and one separate hijack/unauthorized-forwarding case. This grade is bounded to that preserved campaign and endpoint reconstruction; it does not estimate treatment-leakage prevalence in other benchmarks or prove the corrected codebook uniquely captures every security construct.

independent_checks.logical_consistency_result: The sealed FE-355 summary matches the primary arXiv record on direct treatment leakage, the fixed-behavior treatment-only class flip, the 31-label counterfactual change, the 58-of-70 treatment-blind reclassification, the zero ATTACK_SUCCESS corrected census, and preservation of three verified protected-data transfers plus one separate hijack/forwarding case. The treatment-only flip is strong causal evidence that the historical endpoint was not treatment-invariant, but the audit is author-run and campaign-bounded, and the paper explicitly does not claim a population attack rate, model ranking, defense efficacy estimate, or uniquely correct semantic codebook.

grading.causal_attribution: strong_for_direct_treatment_metadata_leakage_in_the_historical_endpoint; fixed behavior with treatment-only relabeling changes class
grading.independent_replication: not_established; the reconstruction and blinded concordance checks are within the same study and the paper states this is not an independent third-party annotation study
grading.reproducibility: strong_for_the_preserved finite campaign and deterministic reconstruction; external cross-benchmark reproduction was not independently verified in this slice
grading.primary_source_support: strong; the arXiv record directly reports the treatment-derived gate, fixed-behavior flip, 31 changed ATTACK_SUCCESS labels, 58-of-70 benign reclassifications, corrected zero ATTACK_SUCCESS census, and retained security-relevant cases
grading.uncertainty: The evidence strongly supports the narrow methodological failure that a reproducible security label can be causally driven by treatment identity rather than unauthorized behavior when the endpoint consumes treatment-derived metadata. It does not establish how common this defect is in other agent-security benchmarks, whether all endpoint proxies can be detected by the paper's linter, or that the locked v2 codebook is uniquely semantically correct at every construct boundary.

phase1_acceptance_boundary: FE-355 contributes strong campaign-bounded evidence for an aggregate false-completion/measurement-integrity guard: a security endpoint should be invariant to treatment identity when executed behavior is held fixed and should require unauthorized behavioral predicates rather than experiment metadata. It does not by itself eliminate any Work/protected/manual execution dependency, prove a zero-quota Chat-native outcome route, establish 18/18 current-pool coverage, satisfy replay/resume or scheduler-persistence gates, or close the Phase-1 root.
